articles.title: Ephemeral Testing
articles.summary: Ephemeral testing is a method of ensuring software quality by testing the software component that is built on top of a library, rather than directly assessing the original work. This approach allows developers to simulate different layers of functionality and identify potential issues before building the core code. By using ephemeral testing, developers can create a library with a clean API, stable invariants, and useful errors, and then test it to see how well the agent produces something that works quickly. This approach can be particularly useful for AI programming, where building the core code can be time-consuming and uncertain.

This hints that in a compute-rich regime, we might be able to surpass backprop.
